t: Day twenty-four. The frost on the window still says three x plus four is twenty-five.
It's the time of the freeze. If we solve for x, the Rewinder lands at the exact second.
The moment before is behind five locks. Every lock is an equation. Solve it, and it opens.
Five locks? I solved a jar of pickles once. Took me a week.
Go. Bring him back. Or at least bring back his sentence.
Lock one. Read it as a machine. x went in. It was times three. Then plus four. Out came twenty-five.
So we go backwards! Divide by three first! Twenty-five divided by three is eight and a third. Lever!
Why is it dark? Why is Mr. Dunmore singing to a mop?
Eight and a third. Eight twenty at night. You undid the times before the plus.
I'm going to pretend I never saw this. He's really good, though.
Last thing done, first thing undone. The last thing was plus four. So we undo that first.
Undo plus four: take four. Twenty-five take four is twenty-one.
Undo times three: divide by three. Twenty-one divided by three is seven.
x is seven!
Check it. Put seven back in. Three times seven is twenty-one. Plus four is twenty-five. It fits.
(softly) Seven. His favourite.
Lock two. Five x minus six is nineteen.
The last thing it did was take away six. So the first thing I do is give six back.
Nineteen plus six is twenty-five. Undo times five: twenty-five divided by five. Five.
Five times five is twenty-five, take six, nineteen. Open.
Lock three. x divided by two, plus three, is ten.
My turn. Last thing: plus three. Undo it: ten take three. Seven.
Then undo the divide by two. The opposite of dividing is... timesing! Seven times two. Fourteen!
Fourteen divided by two is seven, plus three is ten. Marcus, that was perfect.
Write that down. Somewhere official.
Good evening. Day twenty-four of the rain. A frost message has appeared on the school window.
We have a caller.
(on the phone) Chip! It's Marcus. I solved a lock. On purpose. Can that be the headline?
Caller, the headline is the rain. It is always the rain.
Lock four. Two x plus nine is three. That's a strange one. The answer is smaller than the plus.
Undo plus nine. Three take nine. That goes below zero. Minus six.
Undo times two. Minus six divided by two is minus three.
Minus three. Three seconds before. That's where we have to stand.
The last lock has no equation. Just words. The freeze came at second x. Double it, add eleven, and you get twenty-five.
Double it, then add eleven. That's two x plus eleven equals twenty-five.
Undo the eleven: fourteen. Undo the double: seven.
Seven again. It was always going to be seven.
(whispering) Gus. Three seconds before.
He can't see us. This moment is already written.
(whispering) I can, though. I see things backwards. You came from the other end.
He can SEE us?!
(whispering) It's going to rain. It won't stop until someone works it backwards.
Gus, move! It's coming!
(whispering) I know. You can't change it. But you can finish it. Every time you undo something, look for me.
(quietly) The whole sentence. It's going to rain.
Look. The frost. There's a crack in it.
It cracked when we worked it backwards. Every time we undo something, it opens a little more.
Then we keep undoing things. As many as it takes.
Coo.
(to frozen Gus) We heard you, buddy. All of it. We're coming.
So. I opened a lock. I saw the past. I heard the sentence. Am I a sidekick NOW?
(smiling) ...Ask me when he's back.
